mbc1.bank2: 4000-5FFF (2 bits: ROM bits 5-6 or RAM bank)

mbc2.control: 0000-3FFF: address bit 8 clear = RAM enable, set = ROM bank (4 bits, 0 -> 1)

mbc3.ram_bank_or_rtc: 4000-5FFF (0-7 RAM, 8-C RTC S M H DL DH)

mbc7.registers: A000-AFFF while both enables are on, selected by address bits 4-7: Ax0x 0x55 erases the accelerometer latch (X and Y read 0x8000), Ax1x 0xAA then latches the tilt, Ax2x/Ax3x X low/high, Ax4x/Ax5x Y low/high, Ax6x reads 0x00, Ax8x the EEPROM's pins (bit 7 CS, bit 6 CLK, bit 1 DI; bit 0 reads DO); the rest of A000-BFFF reads 0xFF

huc3.mode: 0000-1FFF (low nibble): 0x0 RAM read-only, 0xA RAM read/write, 0xB clock command write, 0xC clock response read, 0xD clock semaphore, 0xE infrared

camera.ram_enable: 0000-1FFF (0x0A enables writes; RAM is always readable)
camera.ram_bank_or_registers: 4000-5FFF: bits 0-3 the RAM bank, bit 4 maps the sensor's registers at A000-BFFF instead
camera.registers: A000 bit 0 starts a capture and reads 1 while it runs (bits 1-2 kept); A001-A035 write-only, read 0x00 (A000-A07F mirrored)

wisdom_tree.bank: a write to 0000-3FFF selects the 32 KiB bank in the low 8 bits of its ADDRESS (the value is ignored); 0000-7FFF is that bank

sachen.base: 0000-1FFF: the base bank, written only while the ROM bank register has bits 4-5 set
sachen.mask: 4000-5FFF: which bank bits come from the base bank, written only while the ROM bank register has bits 4-5 set
sachen.mapping: 0000-3FFF is bank (base AND mask); 4000-7FFF is (bank AND NOT mask) OR (base AND mask); CPU reads of 0100-01FF have address lines A0/A6 and A1/A4 swapped

name: gb_cartridge

provenance.read_for: this card's data and logic, written here

mbc1_multicart.wiring: bank2 drives ROM bits 4-5 and the low register uses 4 bits (bank 0 -> 1 still looks at 5)
mbc1_multicart.note: MBC1M boards (collections) are not marked in the header: the Nintendo logo repeated at bank 0x10's header gives them away

ram_unsized_note: a cartridge type with RAM whose RAM-size byte says none (Blargg's test cartridges) has the smallest RAM chip
sources: Pan Docs (hardware reference: MBCs, MBC7, HuC-3, Game Boy Camera)
Gekkio, Game Boy: Complete Technical Reference
Microchip 93LC56 data sheet (the MBC7's EEPROM protocol)
Antonio Nino Diaz, Game Boy Camera technical information (capture time, registers)
gbdev wiki: Wisdom Tree and Sachen mappers
statement: Cartridge ROM (up to 8 MiB) and RAM (up to 128 KiB) behind a memory bank controller. The header at 0x100-0x14F describes it; `types` maps the cartridge type byte (0x147) to a controller and its features. Two unlicensed boards the header does not name are recognised by where the Nintendo logo is (`unlicensed`).

unlicensed.logo_note: the CRC-32 of the 48-byte Nintendo logo the boot ROM checks at 0x104 (a fingerprint: the logo itself is not stored)
unlicensed.rule: boards the header does not name, recognised when power_on runs (cart_power_on): a Sachen board when the logo is not at 0x104 but is where the boot ROM reads it through the board's scrambled, locked header page; otherwise a Wisdom Tree board when the type byte says ROM only, the logo is at 0x104 and the dump is larger than 32 KiB

sachen.note: the chip holds the header page scrambled; until the boot ROM's logo reads are done the board also forces A7 high (the 'locked' view), so the real logo sits at 0x184-0x1B3 scrambled. The board is unlocked when the boot ROM hands over, which is where the machine starts.

mbc7.eeprom: 93LC56: 128 words of 16 bits, high byte first in cram[0..255]; the save is the unsized RAM every host gives a RAM cartridge (ram_unsized_bytes), so it carries the EEPROM
mbc7.tilt_note: the d-pad tilts the cartridge by 1 g the way it points (right lowers X, up raises Y: things roll that way, checked on Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble); a shell's stick drives the d-pad, and a shell with a real tilt source can add it in tilt_x / tilt_y

huc3.clock: minutes of the day (12 bits) and a day counter (12 bits), kept in the cartridge's clock registers (rtc_s, rtc_m, rtc_h, rtc_dl, rtc_dh) so saves and catch-up are the MBC3's

commands.1: read the nibble at the address, then address + 1
commands.3: write the argument at the address, then address + 1
commands.6: extended: 0 copies the clock to nibbles 00-05 (minutes, days), 1 sets the clock from them, 2 answers 1

huc3.semaphore: mode 0xD reads bit 0 = 1 (ready); writing 0xFE there runs the command (the clock answers at once)
huc3.infrared: mode 0xE reads 0xC0 (no light seen); bit 0 of a write is the LED

camera.sensor_note: no sensor here: the picture is a synthetic scene (camera.card) shaped by what the game writes: exposure time (C, A002-A003) and gain (G, A001 bits 0-4) scale it, edge enhancement (VH A001 bits 5-6, ratio E A004 bits 4-6) sharpens it, I (A004 bit 3) inverts it, and the 4x4 matrix of 3 thresholds (A006-A035) turns it into 2-bit tiles in RAM bank 0 at 0x100; the voltage and offset registers (V, Z, O) are not modelled
